description: Observed mapping from an upstream MCP tool name, through the Omnodex MCP
proxy, to the name the agent makes callable and reports in its hook
payloads. Captured rather than assumed: how an agent treats a character
it cannot put in a tool name is not documented anywhere.

method: tool names was placed behind the proxy, the proxy was registered as
the MCP server 'omnodex', and the agent was asked to print the tool
names it could see, verbatim, without calling any of them.
findings: The proxy joins its prefix verbatim: 'demo' + '__' + the upstream name, whatever characters that name holds.
Claude Code composes 'mcp__' + server + '__' + the proxy's name, again verbatim.
Characters outside [a-zA-Z0-9_-] are NOT rewritten, escaped or normalised. The tool is dropped, silently, and never reaches the model.
A server name may itself contain single underscores, so the server and tool halves can only be split on the FIRST '__' after the 'mcp__' prefix.

tools.note: Dropped. Never offered to the model and never callable.
Dropped, same as '.'. The proxy still lists it upstream.

method: A real routed call in a live session, taken from the append-only log.
This is the pair the correlation has to match: one tool call, seen
once by the hook and once by the proxy.

proxy.session_id: <proxy's own uuid, unrelated to the agent session>

observations: The hook name ends with '__' + the proxy's tool_name exactly.
The parameters are byte-identical, because the proxy forwards the agent's arguments unchanged.
The session ids are unrelated: the proxy mints a fresh uuid per process and never learns the agent's.
The hook is 1.409s earlier. PreToolUse fires before the call reaches the proxy, and the hook's occurred_at is the shim's own clock, so the gap includes subprocess startup.
mcp_server was recorded as 'builtin' because the old regex could not split a server name containing underscores. Fixed alongside this fixture.

note: Attempted on 2026-09-18 with Codex CLI v0.154.0 via `codex exec` and an
`-c mcp_servers.omnodex={...}` override. The proxy was launched (it
wrote a session.started to the event log) but none of its tools,
including the built-in omnodex_status, were offered to the model.
Consistent with Codex requiring a trust or approval step for a new MCP
server before its tools are exposed, which a non-interactive run has no
Needs an interactive Codex session to complete. The correlation does
not depend on this: it matches on the proxy's tool name being a suffix
of the agent's, which holds for any prefix scheme, and assumes only
that the platform does not rewrite characters. That assumption is
measured for Claude Code and unverified for Codex.
